body:
Redline round 3

Reviewed the whole pull request. Rounds 1 to 2 are already on this PR; this run starts at round 3.

The round-2 commits close each of the eight carried findings by refusing the whole class: the main session is approved only for bare script, checks.sh and read-only git command words; variable setters and prefixes are refused; keywords are refused; git runs only at the repository root; the read-flag refusal is widened; sed's script and file operands are read separately; temp patterns get the .. and last-segment rules; and git add accepts an existing bracket-named file. Each fix has deny rows beside its kept neighbours. The setup side (the retired list, --remove-stale, the v2 template and the CLAUDE.md sentence) still reads as sound, and this round raises no new finding. The repository has no scheduled commands or queued jobs, so no changed file shares data with one.

No findings.

### Resolved from earlier rounds

- **R2-1** The main-session approval covers sed, find and the builtins, not only the scripts and read-only git: check_simple now leaves the main session inert for any wrapper, env, timeout or xargs in front of a command and for any command word other than cd, git or a script_name() hit (scripts/redline-guard.sh:986 and :1022); for the roles, sed_script_refused refuses a w, W or e command and a w or e flag on s (:833-948), and find refuses -fprint, -fprint0, -fprintf and -fls (:1143).
- **R2-2** sed -i with -e checks the script as a write target, so a regex holding * or [ is refused: sed_operands (scripts/redline-guard.sh:791-820) separates the script after -e/--expression and the file after -f/--file, in their detached, attached and bundled forms, from the file operands, so only the files reach writable() (:1130).
- **R2-3** The temp-directory exemption for a pattern ignores the `..` segments after the wildcard: writable() now refuses a pattern target that has a .. segment anywhere (scripts/redline-guard.sh:527), and grants the temp-directory exemption only when the text after the cut holds no / (:529-533).
- **R2-4** A file whose name holds [ or { can be edited but never staged: git add refuses it as a pattern: The git add branch checks a path that holds a pattern character as a literal path when a file of exactly that name exists (scripts/redline-guard.sh:1282-1283), so an existing [id].php can be staged and still goes through the protected and ask-rule checks.
- **R2-5** A leading `!` or shell keyword hides the next command from the guard, and the main session is now approved for it: ! and the shell keywords left BUILTINS and are refused as a command word through KEYWORDS (scripts/redline-guard.sh:723 and :1025); the main session is inert for them because of the bare-command-word rule at :1022.
- **R2-6** GIT_* and other variables reach git and the approved scripts by export, bash -c and BASH_ENV: Every NAME=value prefix, bare or after env, goes through prefix_refused on every simple command, not only on git, and only REDLINE_OCTANE and the checks.json vars with a plain-word value are exempt (scripts/redline-guard.sh:967-998). Every env option is refused (:993), and export, declare, typeset, set, readonly and local are refused as commands (:1028).
- **R2-7** git grep -O gets past read_flag_refused when abbreviated or bundled: read_flag_refused now refuses any word that starts with --op and any single-dash bundle that holds O (scripts/redline-guard.sh:1213), which covers the abbreviated and bundled spellings of -O.
- **R2-8** git -C into a temp directory runs a program its .git/config names: The person chose option A: check_git refuses every subcommand unless the working directory, after -C and any cd, is REPO or REPO_REAL (scripts/redline-guard.sh:1235-1237), so git never runs in a repository whose config a role could have written.
